clusters.body:
<!-- impact:dwm-wpf:Config2 -->

Impact analysis conducted on source code version:

- https://github.com/defrances/HostApplication - commit `22b249a754b849dac151e976b533f60994fc6098`

## Updates applicable for this product configuration

| Title | Package | CVEs | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Microsoft DWM Core Library Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5093998](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-45637) | CVE-2026-45637 | Install - High Prio |
| Desktop Window Manager Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability | [KB5099535](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-50692) | CVE-2026-50692 | Install - High Prio |

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config2`
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`
- OS: `Windows 11 IoT Enterprise` build `10.0.26100.4200`
- Clinical criticality: `high`
- Network exposure: `restricted_lan`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `M` | `H` |
| Product | `M` | `L` | `L` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

HostApplication.csproj sets `UseWPF=true`. MainWindow.xaml defines the primary Window chrome and layout. app.manifest enables `dpiAware` true/pm and `dpiAwareness` PerMonitorV2, which routes composition through DWM.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** CI publishes `--self-contained true` for `win-x64` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and no `PackageReference` loads the patched Windows component inside HostApplication.exe.
- **If we install: App may break.** Desktop Window Manager patches can alter composition or elevation surfaces that WPF uses for PerMonitorV2 DPI. Visual layout in MainWindow.xaml should be checked after install and reboot.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** Skipping leaves DWM elevation-of-privilege class issues on the host while the WPF client in MainWindow.xaml can still run.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Current `main` already runs on today's host bits; installing the KB does not replace the bundled .NET 9 runtime inside the published exe.

### Conclusions

This cluster couples the vendor patch to Host Application through cited product files on `main`. The OS KB does not patch the self-contained runtime embedded in the CI publish output; validation focus is host behavior around Desktop Window Manager (DWM Core), not a missing product NuGet dependency.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-45637, CVE-2026-50692 in Desktop Window Manager (DWM Core). SBOM scan and source code scan revealed there is no direct import of that Windows component in HostApplication.Core or the WPF project; the product runs on the host stack that receives the KB.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Affected functions:** WPF UI rendering and DPI (`MainWindow.xaml`, app.manifest PerMonitorV2).
- **Hazards:** Host-level issues outside the published exe; no new in-process dependency on the patched library.
- **Install vs skip:** Install may require reboot and targeted smoke; skip leaves host Desktop Window Manager (DWM Core) exposure while the product process can still start.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- None. No documented test covers this coupling.

### Gap Analysis

- None identified for documented Core tests; no UI automation covers WPF layout after OS graphics patches.

## Recommendation

Install - High Prio for lab validation tracking on `Config2`. This email is not authorization to deploy to production.

## Product Configuration Specification

- Product configuration: `Config2`
- Model / role: `LabBench-L110` / `lab-analysis-workstation`
- Deployment group: `lab-ring-0`

## Vendor vs product scores

| | Severity | Likelihood | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendor | `H` | `L` | `H` |
| Product | `M` | `M` | `M` |

## Technical Impact Assessment

### Impacted Components

NoteStore.cs reads and writes `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt` via `File.ReadAllText`, `File.WriteAllText`, and `Directory.CreateDirectory`. MainViewModel.cs calls `_noteStore.Load()` / `Save()` on user action. TC-SMOKE-NOTES locks the round-trip contract.

### Potential Risks

- **Required for the app to keep working: Not required.** CI publishes `--self-contained true` for `win-x64` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, and no `PackageReference` loads the patched Windows component inside HostApplication.exe.
- **If we install: App may break.** An NTFS servicing update replaces kernel filter behavior on the volume holding the user profile; file APIs in NoteStore.cs should be re-run under TC-SMOKE-NOTES after reboot.
- **If we skip: Station stays exposed.** NTFS remote-code-execution class flaws can remain on the host volume that stores notes.txt while the application process continues to use the same paths.
- **Compatibility: Compatible with the app.** Current `main` already runs on today's host bits; installing the KB does not replace the bundled .NET 9 runtime inside the published exe.

### Conclusions

This cluster couples the vendor patch to Host Application through cited product files on `main`. The OS KB does not patch the self-contained runtime embedded in the CI publish output; validation focus is host behavior around NTFS on the user profile volume, not a missing product NuGet dependency.

## Cybersecurity impact assessment

This patch fixes CVE-2026-50448 in NTFS on the user profile volume. SBOM scan and source code scan revealed there is no direct import of that Windows component in HostApplication.Core or the WPF project; the product runs on the host stack that receives the KB.

## Product Risk assessment

- **Affected functions:** Local notes persistence (`NoteStore.cs`, `MainViewModel.SaveNotes`).
- **Hazards:** Host-level issues outside the published exe; no new in-process dependency on the patched library.
- **Install vs skip:** Install may require reboot and targeted smoke; skip leaves host NTFS on the user profile volume exposure while the product process can still start.

## Test Planning

### Recommended Regression Suite

- TC-SMOKE-NOTES — save/load round-trip on the notes file path.

### Gap Analysis

- None identified for documented Core tests; no UI automation covers WPF layout after OS graphics patches.

## Recommendation

Install - High Prio for lab validation tracking on `Config2`. This email is not authorization to deploy to production.

findings.title: Vendor bulletin HTTPS accepts any server certificate
findings.evidence: On main, `src/HostApplication.Core/InsecureVendorBulletinClient.cs` requires `sslPolicyErrors == SslPolicyErrors.None` in `AcceptAnyServerCertificate` (no `INTENTIONAL_SKILL_TEST_VULNERABILITY` marker; `Marker` is `TLS_CERTIFICATE_VALIDATED`). `TC-REG-TLS-CALLBACK` asserts invalid chains are rejected. Repo `docs/mds2.md` MDS2-TLS text is stale versus this code; catalog Status/Countermeasure cells are stale.

findings.title: Notes stored as plaintext in user AppData
findings.evidence: `src/HostApplication.Core/NoteStore.cs` persists UTF-8 plaintext under `%AppData%\HostApplication\notes.txt` only; inputs MDS2-DATA is met (local notes, no PHI, no remote storage). Residual risk is host-account access to the file.

findings.title: No inbound network listener
findings.evidence: Architecture and inputs MDS2-NET: single optional outbound HTTPS GET via `InsecureVendorBulletinClient.FetchAsync`; no `TcpListener`/`HttpListener` in the codebase on main.
